In BHS I have noted a single case, not wholly certain, of anyatra as preposition with instr. (as in Pali, instead of abl. as in Skt.): rātriṃdivaṃ bhavantībhir nānyā kathā kāryā, anyatra nṛttagītavāditena, you are to say nothing else, except dance, song, and instrumental music (?). But the adverbial use in this mg., so rare in Skt. and not recorded for Pali, is well established in BHS; in the following cases the form and construction of other words in the clause is totally unaffected by anyatra; often it may be translated as if it were a conjunction, except that … It almost always follows a negative expression (or interrogative, rhetorically equivalent to neg.); and this is sometimes resumed by an additional na before anyatra (as in the last case under 1, above): sārthaṃ na paśyati nānyatra gardabhayānam eva, he didnʼt see the caravan, not except only a donkey-cart; and with anyatra as quasi-conjunction, nāsti anyo upāyo nānyatra etaṃ samudraṃ utsicāmi, there is no other means, not (any) except (that) I bale out (exhaust) this sea. In the next the na before anyatra goes with the main verb (or rather ppp.): nānyatra sattvānāṃ paripācanārtham avatāraṇārtham ete dharmaparyāyā bhāṣitāḥ, these dharmaparyāya are not spoken except (i.e. are spoken only) to mature creatures and make them arrive at comprehension. Otherwise, after negs.: (nānyaḥ … saṃvidyate ya etāṃ gaṇanāṃ prajānāty) anyatrāhaṃ vā yo vā syān mādṛśaḥ, except (it be) I or someone like me; na ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃstavaṃ karoty anyatropasaṃkrāntānāṃ … dharmaṃ bhāṣate, and he has no association with them, except that … he preaches the Law to them when they come to him; similarly; yūyaṃ ca śabdaṃ na śṛṇotha mahyaṃ, anyatra so nirvṛtu lokanāthaḥ, and you do (would) not listen to my words, except (i.e. unless; sc. you believed that) the Lord of the World has entered nirvāṇa; (na ca … nānātvam asty) anyatra … saṃkhyāṃ gacchanti, except that …; (a passage badly misunderstood by; e.g. in 7 read 'dharmā = adharmāḥ) na lakṣaṇataḥ kalpyāḥ (delete daṇḍa) te 'nyatra saṃvyavahārārthā abhidhīyante, they (impossibilities like the son of a barren woman) are not conceivable by way of characteristic marks, except that (? or possibly on the contrary, to 1) they are spoken of as terms of common use (they have existence only as words); anyatra … vibhāvyate, except that it is discussed … (after neg.); after interrog., kānyā putrasya gatir anyatra mātāpitarāv eva, what other recourse could there be for a son (i.e. there could be none), except his parents; no negative (except by vague implication), (annādyaṃ parikṣīṇam) anyatra … ekā mānikā … avaśiṣṭā, (edible things were destroyed, i.e. there were none), except that … one mānikā was left; (see s.v. upādāya 1 d).

(= Pali id.), (1) knows by abhijñā, q.v. The technical Buddhist meaning of the noun is certainly at times associated with the verb, which in Skt. means knows in a very general way. The extent to which the special Buddhist sense is present in the verb is often doubtful; I list a few cases where it seems pretty clear: abhijānāmi (and, remember, I think wrongly);;;. The translation remember, also given, is due to the fact that events of the past are often referred to; but I think the Buddha (the usual subject in such cases) knows them by supernatural knowledge or so-called intuition (abhijñā, q.v.), not by memory; (2) recognizes (as a duty), takes upon oneself (a vow or undertaking); so also in Pali, e.g. (definitions in Pali dictionaries including hardly do justice to this mg.): abhijānāmy ahaṃ … ekam evādvitīyaṃ kolam āhāram āhartum, I undertake to allow myself to eat only a single kola as food; similarly.

(= Pali abhiññā), higher or supernatural knowledge; intuition (). There are 5 or 6, in both Pali and BHS, agreeing in essence tho the order and precise forms of the names vary. In, five: divyacakṣus, divyaśrotra, paracittajñāna, pūrvanivāsānusmṛti, ṛddhi; in six, same order, with variant forms, (parasya) cetaḥ- (citta-)-paryāya- (q.v.)-jñāna, for the third; the sixth is āśravakṣayajñāna, as in Pali and elsewhere when 6 are named; the fifth is ṛddhividhijñāna in; lists 5, practically as in except that the fifth is ṛddhivimokṣakriyā, an unusual phrase, for which no v.l. is given in or; () cites his ms. as reading ṛddhisākṣātkriyā, which is much more plausible. Twenty abhijñā-karmāṇi are set forth in detail. In the abhijñā, collectively, are classified as to their origin in four ways (in l. 16 read with te 'bhijñā na vipākajāḥ). (in Skt. rare and only Vedic; = Pali ˚sīdati), sits down: (kīdṛśena) yānena kumāro ˚dati, in what vehicle does the prince (= is he to) sit?; aor. ˚ṣīdi, em. ˚ṣīde (m.c.); in ger. abhiniṣadya in caus. sense, having seated (or with consacré), bodhisattvo maitreyaṃ … tuṣitabhavane 'bhiniṣadya (to take his own place after his descent to earth); abhiniṣaṇṇaḥ, sat down,.
, nt. (= Pali abhinikkhamaṇa; to next), departure from worldly life, entrance into ascetic life:;;;;;, etc., common.
(= Pali abhinikkhamati), enters ascetic life:;;;;;;, etc., common. (Also as in Skt., goes forth, in any secular sense, as udyānabhūmim to a pleasure park,; udyānam.)

(not in Skt. in this sense; in Pali, in this sense, only caus. abhinipphādeti), gets, secures, obtains: ˚dyeta (cīvaraṃ); ˚dyamāna(ḥ), in (while) obtaining (trying to obtain, sc. a robe); ppp. abhiniṣpanne cīvare;.
(= Pali abhinippīḷeti), ppp. ˚pīḍita-, squeezed out, got out with difficulty: ˚ta-spaṣṭapadām (human speech, by a deer).

(caus. of *abhi-niṣ-piṣ-), crushes utterly: ˚yan, pres. pple.,; Tib. cited as phye mar (into powder) glog ciṅ (? glog cited only as noun, lightning; here it seems to mean crush); same Tib. for niṣpīṣanto.
(nt.; cf. Skt. abhiniṣyandate, very rare), irrigation, infiltration (as) with moisture: cittanagarābhiniṣyandanaprayuktena te … bhavitavyaṃ sarvatathāgatadharmameghasaṃpratīcchanatayā.
, adj., = abhinīla:, of eyes, one of the 32 lakṣaṇa. But 2d ed. ˚nīla.
, adj. (= Pali id.; once in Skt.,), very dark, of eyes (29th of the 32 lakṣaṇa, q.v.) and hair: (eyes);;;; (here ˚netra-gopakṣmā, see gopakṣman);;; (hair);.
, read abhindan (pres. pple.) sroto, not breaking the (surface of the) water:, repeated; cf. s.v. abhijjamāna.]
, adj. (cf. bhid, 8), not seduced, not won (amorously, of a woman, by a man): (vs) kā tuhyam abhinna (so mss.; em. abhukta, which is right in sense) varteyā, what woman could you not seduce?
, adv. after (others), last (of all), or [Page054-a] temporally, too late, tvam abhi˚ āgatā. But probably read with v.l. atipaścāt = Pali atipacchā (graphic confusion of t and bh).
, nt., n. of a cetiya (caitya) in the south:; in the {{parellel->parallel||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} Padma (6).
(= Pali Ahipāraka), n. of a minister:
(= Pali abhippa˚; once in Skt.,), bestrews (often after adhyavakirati, q.v., or abhyava˚): ˚kirati; ˚kiranti;;;;; ger. ˚kiritvā;; ppp. ˚kīrṇa.

; ppp. ˚ṇata, stretched out towards: (śākhā … nimnagām abhipraṇatābhavat); caus. abhipraṇamayati, extends, holds out (= praṇāmayati, q.v., cf. also praṇamati, ˚mayati): (vs) abhiprāṇamayetsuḥ, aor. (burning brands, towards a pyre); ā perh. m.c. (or augment?).
(cf. Skt. pradakṣiṇī-karoti and abhipradakṣiṇaṃ karoti), passes around keeping on the right (respectfully): pres. p. n. pl. ˚karontā; ger. ˚kṛtvā id. 17.
, m., or ˚nā (cf. Pali abhippamoda), great joy: (prose) ˚nān, acc. pl.; (prose) ˚nā, n. sg.
(nt.; cf. abhiprayuṅkte, Vedic only), possession: ˚nāya, dat.,.
(m.; cf. next), hanging down (noun): (prose) samabhāgābhipralamba-racita-śākhaḥ (of a tree).

(= Pali abhippalambati), hangs down (intrans.): ˚te;, here with ālambate and adhyāl˚, of lengthening shadows falling on earth at evening (same context in Pali abhippal˚, subject chāyā, with loc. paṭhaviyā); pres. pple. ˚bamānāni; ppp. ˚bita, hanging down, (aṣṭau yojanaśatāny) abhipralambita-śākhāpattrapalāśaḥ (bodhivṛkṣaḥ); behung (with), having … suspended upon them, at end of cpds. preceded by names of articles suspended,;;;;;; (in this mg. perhaps derived from caus.?); caus. ˚bayanti they hang (trans.), cause to be suspended (acc., from, abl.), (gaganatalāt puṣpapaṭṭadāmāni); (puṣpadāmāni); pres. pple. ˚bayantyo.
(nt.; to Skt. ˚varṣati), act of raining down: -vṛṣṭy-abhi˚;; dharmavṛṣṭy-abhi˚;; dharmasalilābhipravarṣaṇa-tayā, because of state-of-raining-down the flood of dharma.
(cf. prec.), one who causes to rain down: ˚tāro dharmaśravaṇameghānām.
, makes resound or play (musical instruments) in honor of someone: devadundubhim ˚dayām āsus tasya … satkārārtham; (divyāni vādyāni).

(ppp. of ˚sīdati, q.v.: Pali abhippa˚), favorably disposed, with gen., loc. with or without antike, or at end of cpds.; in Pali and BHS also believing in, religiously, see esp.; croyant parfaitement,; the two mgs. often hardly distinguishable: (brāhmaṇeṣv); (ye Māraputrā bodhisattve); (bhikṣūṇāṃ, bhikṣusya);;;; (brāhmaṇeṣu); (śramaṇānām); (mama, sc. a hermit); ˚na-citta (see s.v. ˚sīdati); (asmākam);, and an-abhi˚;;; [Page054-b] (śaraṇaṃ gatām ˚sannām);; (bhagavato 'ntike cittam ˚sannam); (buddhe); (bhagavantaṃ … dṛṣṭvā cāsya cittam ˚sannaṃ);; buddhadharmasaṃghābhi˚; but also lūhābhi˚, with lūhādhimukta, inclined to what is mean or base,.
(in this sense app. not recorded), sets out towards: himavantam abhiprasaresi (aor.); ppp. ˚sṛta having come into, ˚sṛtair … salilapravāhair (that had flowed in).

(m., to next, or its caus.; cf. abhiprasanna; Pali abhipassāda, said to mean only faith, belief), either the making well-disposed, or the making to believe: an-abhiprasannānām abhiprasādāya; buddhaśāsanābhiprasādārthaṃ, in order to make well-disposed, or believing (in).

(= Pali abhippa˚; in Skt. only caus. ˚sādayati, makes well disposed), favors, is well disposed (to), conceives faith (in, gen. or acc.): (sarvajanakāyo etasya) ṛṣisya (viz. the Buddha) sahasraparivārasya … ˚diṣyati; (bodhisattvapiṭakaṃ … śrutvā ca) punar ˚dati; caus., makes well disposed to, or makes to believe in, ˚sādayanti Yaśodasya mātāpitarau bhagavato santike cittaṃ, … made their hearts favorable to (prob. = believing in) the Bhagavat Cf. abhiprasanna, ˚sāda.

, m., difference: (na …) kaścid viśeṣo vā 'bhiprāyo vā nānākaraṇaṃ vā. Based on use of Pali adhippāya (= Skt. abhiprāya) intention, but also difference; on the latter mg. see s.v. The old Buddhist word adhippāya was Sktized, keeping this new mg. in addition to its normal Skt. mg. Compare with passage the Pali, ko viseso ko adhippāyo kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ.
, adj. (intensifying to priya; cf. s.v. abhi 1, d), quite agreeable: yathā brāhmaṇapariṣāye abhipriyan (em. abhiprāyan; but for this ˚prāyas, ˚prāyo would be expected) tathā bhavatu.

(for ˚te, pass.; no cpd. of abhi-budh is recorded in Skt. or Pali, except rarely the noun abhibuddhi, on which see), becomes enlightened: (vs; no v.l.) drakṣyāmy abhibudhyato bodhiṃ, I shall behold the enlightenment of him as he is becoming enlightened.

, nt., feeding upon (to Pali abhibhakkhayitvā); so prob. read with 1 ms. in ekaṃ mṛgaṃ visarjayiṣyāmaḥ, mahārājasya ca mṛgamānsena abhibhakṣaṇaṃ (v.l. avikṣaṇam; em. avibhakṣaṇaṃ, supposed to mean non-cessation de nourriture; implausible) bhaviṣyati, ime ca mṛgā evaṃ anayavyasanaṃ nopapadyiṣyanti, we will let go one deer (every day), and the king will feed on deer-meat, and (at the same time) thus these deer will not get into serious trouble. Less likely is the v.l. avikṣaṇaṃ = AMg. avikkhaṇa (by false Sktization) = Pali (an-)apekkhana, Skt. (rare) apekṣaṇa = apekṣā desire (at the same time the king will crave deer-meat, and these deer …).

(not recorded in this physical sense; Skt. and Pali only overcomes and the like), mounts, climbs upon or over; passes over: (vs) (mīḍhaṃgirī …) abhibhūya caṅkramati tatra ca nopalipto; (vs) kuḍyā ca vṛkṣa abhibhūya, (the Buddhaʼs radiance, ābhā) passing over walls and trees (leaves no shadow).
(cf. Skt. abhibhāti), perhaps appearance, in yathābhibhānaṃ, adj. (or adv.?), something like immediately evident?: ˚naṃ ca na duḥpṛcchayā … pratiṣṭhitaṃ (textually uncertain).

, adj. or subst. (to Skt. abhibhavati), overcoming: ananta-pariṣad-abhibhāvanaḥ, ep. of Bodhisattvas (Bhvr.? or Tatpur.? in the latter case is abhi˚ adj. or n. ag.?); ˚na-tā, state of overcoming, (prose).
, ppp. ˚ṣita (in this sense not recorded), promise(d): (vs) dadāhi nas tāta yathābhibhāṣitaṃ (no v.l.) … yānāni, give us, father, as (you) promised, cars, etc.
(not in Pali; in Skt. once pass. abhibhidya-,), splits: ˚bhindyāt, opt.
(f.; not in this sense in Pali; = abhibhvāyatana, q.v.), supremacy: abhibhuvas … aṣṭau (comm. abhibhvāyatana); sarvalokābhibhū (Bhvr.),.
, n. of a future Buddha: n. sg. ˚yaśo (so mss.; em. ˚bhūyaśo, perhaps rightly).
, nt. (= Pali abhibhāyatana), sphere of sovereignty, one of the eight stages of mastery over the senses (in jhāna,); also called abhibhū, q.v., in BHS: (listed in);, comm.; xx—xxi.44, comm.

, with acc. or dat. (loc.?), in, used four times of the attitude of a husband or wife towards a very ugly spouse; perhaps is hostile towards (as in Skt.), but despises, contemns, or perhaps loathes would seem more natural: (14) anyam-anyam (15) ˚yanti, … patiṃ ˚yati, (16) … patiḥ pāparūpāye bhāryāye abhimanyati, (17) … yā te putra nābhimanyiṣyati. Cf. next.

(to Skt. ˚manyate, BHS ˚ti), injuriousness, seeking to do harm: jñānenā 'bhi˚ (prose); could be em. to avamany˚, cf. avamanyati, mss. atimanyanatā, em. ava˚. But cf. where probably read parānabhimanyanatāyai for parābhimanyatāyai (by em.; mss. parābhigamanyatāyai, parāgamanatāyai; Calc. as).

, adj. (from Skt. and Pali abhimāna, in two different mgs.; cf. ābhi˚), (1) proud, conceited: (prose); (prose), 5 (vs);; (2) holding an erroneous view: (could be interpreted as ābhi˚) nāsty-asti-tvābhimānikasya.
(cf. Skt. and Pali ˚māna), pride: jāty-abhimānikā-nirabhimānatāyai, to make prideless their pride of birth.
, n. of the 6th of the 10 Bodhisattvabhūmi:;;; etc.
, n. of a monk of old (previous incarnation of Śākyamuni): (A transl. of his story,, by,).

(to Skt. abhiyācati; cf. Skt. satyābhiyācana, adj., making requests true, s.v.), entreaty: ˚nāṃ viditvā; in satyābhiyācanayā with appeal to truth = satya-vacana, q.v., Pali saccakiriyā, solemn declaration by the truth of something (in spoken by Buddha in effecting a miracle; see).
, adj.-ppp. (= Skt. ˚yukta), zealous, intent, (mentally) applied: āśayena … abhiyuktakā(ḥ). May be m.c.

(also ˚ti; orig. pass. of Skt. abhi-yuj), (is yoked;) yokes oneself; fig. applies oneself (to, loc.; or absolutely): (prose) abhiyujyadhve, you are yoked, harnessed (to the vehicles just mentioned; wrongly and); (tathāgataśāsane) 'bhiyujyante, apply themselves; abhiyujyatha (gauraveṇa), apply yourselves!
, f. ˚ikā, adj. (= Pali abhiratta; Skt. ˚rakta not in this sense), (very) red: (vs) tālukā cā 'bhiraktikā (perhaps m.c.).
(m.?), of unknown mg.: yena saptābhiraṅgā ca. The whole passage is obscure.
, ppp. of *abhiracayati: prepared, arranged, fixed up: (vs) mayābhiracitam yad idam tvadarthe.
, n. of a lokadhātu, where dwells the Buddha Akṣobhya: (located in the east);;.

(Pali allegedly abhiramma, Maung Tin, see; Ap. ahiramma,; see an-, nirabhi˚), pleasing: sarvamanāpāni copasaṃhartavyāni viṣayābhiramyāṇi; Tib. yul ñams dgaḥ ba thams cad ni sbyor cig, apparently making viṣaya (yul) subject of upasaṃhartavyāni, and not translating abhi˚. The sense must apparently be all-mind-charming and pleasing objects of sense are to be collected (prepared, for the prince to enjoy); yathābhiramyam (= Pali yathābhirantam), adv., as long as is agreeable:.

(m.? to Skt. abhi-rādh-; cf. next two), winning: (prose) … bodhisattvasya buddhā(ḥ) … abhirādhacittā bhavanti: but prob. read abhirāddha- (Skt.) with citation of the passage, the Buddhas have minds favorably disposed towards …]
(cf. prec. and next; Skt. ˚dhana, Pali an-abhirādhana), winning favor, conciliation:.
, adj. (gdve. to Pali abhirādheti = sādhayati, see; Skt. abhirādhayati, only propitiates, wins the favor of; cf. prec. two), to be won, attained: -abhirādhyā guṇavibhūtis.
, n. of a girl attendant on Subhadrā (1):.
, adj. (= Skt. and Pali ˚ta), in yathābhirucitakam, adv., as one pleases: (prose; not dimin.).
(in Skt. only ppp. ˚rudita; not in Pali), laments: ger. ˚rudya.

(so with 1 ms.) or ˚hana (so v.l.; = Pali abhirūhana; cf. abhirohaṇa; to Skt. abhirohati), mounting, ascent: abhirūha(na)saṃpannāḥ (sattvāḥ, sc. Bodhisattvas; in Pali lit. or fig. of mounting as on a ship, esp. by a gangplank; so presumably here, fig. furnishing a gangplank to salvation).
(= Pali ˚ti; not in this sense in Skt.), surpasses (lit. outshines): (sumeruḥ parvatarājaḥ sarvān kulaparvatān abhibhavann) abhirocate ca samabhirocate coccatvena vipulatvena ca.

(nt.; to prec.), {{ng->surpassing||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} brilliance, splendor:;, in adj. cpd. (sarva-)sattvābhirocanāṃ, having the splendor of all beings, or, illuminating all beings (of a divinity); (prose) ˚nasabhāgatām.
(nt.; Sktized form of abhirūhana, see abhirūha), mounting (on a ship or other vehicle): yānabhūtaṃ sarvabodhisattvābhirohaṇatayā, because all Bodhisattvas mount upon it.
, adj. (app. cpd. of abhi, intensive, with lakṣaṇa; Bhvr.), having superior appearance, fine looking (of grass growing on the place of bodhi):.

(orig. ppp. of Skt. abhi-lakṣ-; = Pali abhilakkhita, see), distinguished; in Pali often with abhiññāta renowned, and so in BHS with abhijñāta, of the place of bodhi;, of a king (mss. abhirakṣito, em.); ˚ta-puruṣa-, distinguished men; ˚tāyā(ḥ), and ˚tāyāṃ (with mss.), of the mother of a Bodhisattva in his last rebirth;; abhilakṣitātmanām, of distinguished persons.
(only in śakrābhi˚, q.v.), fixed upon, worn by (Tib. on thogs pa, presumably to ḥdogs pa, tie or fasten on).
, = Tib. mṅon par brjod pa, full expression, elucidation (); not Geschwätzigkeit ().

(rare except in neg. anabhi˚, nirabhi˚, qq.v.), expressible, that can be put in words: ˚pya-vastu; ˚pyāḥ svabhāvā dharmāṇām. In the prose Introduction to, line 2, reads paraṃparābhilāpyānabhilāpya-buddhakṣetra-, but the true reading is paraṃparānabhilāpyānabhi˚ with v.l. and; see anabhilāpyānabhilāpya.
(not elsewhere recorded in this sense), touches lightly, grazes, with acc.: (elephants abhilikhanti the feet of Śuddhodana with the tips of their trunks).
, adj. (= Skt. ˚līna; cf. abhinilīnaka), lived in (by birds): (prose) kākābhi˚, of an old house; perhaps pejorative -ka.
(abhi with Skt. ḍī), flies thither: ˚yathā (mss., em. ˚ta) (=, where ni-lī˚ is read, see nilīyati).
, ifc. (adj.? or n. act., in Bhvr. cpd.? to Skt. abhi-lokayati), seeing: (vs) bahudharmaśatābhilokane … cakṣuṣi (nt. acc. dual).
, adj. (abhi, intensive, with Skt. vatsala), very affectionate:.
, adj. (= Skt. ˚varṣin, Pali ˚vassi), raining, pouring down: (vs) amṛtābhivarṣikāḥ, n. pl. m. (-ka m.c.?).

(Skt. in this sense only non-caus. ˚vahati, chiefly Vedic; Pali abhivāheti, removes, puts away), causes to be brought near: (vs), read, śūra bhūta abhivāhayāhi me, cause true heroes to be brought to me; (vs) dharmayānam ˚yāhi me.
, adj. (abhi, intensive, and Skt. vicitrita), highly embellished: and (prose) ratnavṛkṣābhi˚; (prose) -ratnavastuśatābhi˚.

(Pali abhiviññāpeti only, object methunaṃ dhammaṃ, makes manifest = consummates; Skt. only non-caus. abhivijānāti, perceives), (1) lit. makes perceptible (by sound), and so makes to resound, with acc. object and instr. svareṇa (śabdena); the common mg. in BHS: (prose) lokaṃ svareṇābhivijñāpayati; (vs) lokadhātuṃ svareṇa … abhivijñăpeyā (opt.); lokadhātuḥ svareṇābhivijñāpto 'bhūd; mahānagaraṃ śabdenābhivijñăptam abhūt; svareṇa abhivijñāpitam; svareṇa abhivijñāpayati; lokadhātuḥ svareṇābhivijñăpto (wrongly instructed); buddhasvareṇābhivijñāpayantam (pres. pple.); (2) makes perceptible (visually), makes manifest: pres. pass. pple. abhivijñăpyamānāni, being manifested, (sarvārambaṇāni), 6 (sarvabodhisattvaparṣanmaṇḍalāni).
(not in Pali; Skt. only ppp. ˚nīta), trains completely: fut. pple. ˚neṣyan; ger. ˚netvā (mss., em. ˚neti).
(not in Pali or Pkt.; Skt. once ˚lokya, ger.,, see), gazes intently at, examines closely (with acc.): ˚kayati; ˚keti;; pres. pple. ˚kayanto; ˚kento; ˚kayan; ger. ˚ketvā; all prose except. Cf. prec.

(abhi with Skt. viśrā˚), gives away in largess: pass., read abhyavakīryante (best mss.) smābhiviśrāṇyante (certainly intended, tho acc. to not supported in mss.; text ˚śrāmyante which is nonsense); so Tib., mṅon par (= abhi) byin no (give).
, doubtful reading, (vs); if correct, must mean dwelling; who dwelt, Skt. abhyuṣita, to otherwise unrecorded *abhi-vasati: devata ˚ta bodhimaṇḍesmin.
, nt. (substantivized ppp. of Skt. abhivṛṣ), what is rained (upon); rain: meghābhivṛṣṭena, by reason of the rain of the clouds upon (them).
(in comp.; to Pali abhivedeti), experience, suffering (of pain): (prose) duḥkhābhivedanābhinunnasya.
, ppp. (to abhi with denom. *vyūhayati to Skt. vyūha), festively adorned: (prose) mārgo 'bhivyūhito 'bhūt.

, rarely ˚dhayati (?), (= Pali abhisaddahati, always with single s, pointing to a new MIndic prefixation of abhi; not in Skt.), believes, with gen. of person, acc. of thing (as in Pali): ˚dadhāti;;; ˚dadhāsi (bhagavataḥ); ˚dadhāmi (etaṃ); ˚dadhati (3 pl.); ˚dadhasi (bhagavataḥ); ˚dadhanti (prose; tathāgatasya); ˚dhayanti (prose; v.l. ˚dadhanti); opt. ˚dadheta (sūtram); impv. ˚dadhadhvam (tathāgatasya); fut. ˚dadhāsyati; ˚dadhāsyanti;;; ˚dadhāsye (1 sg. mid.); ˚dadhiṣyanti; ppp. ˚dadhāta; gdve. ˚dadhitavya.
(n. act. from prec., with suffix ana plus -tā,; not from Sanskritic pres. mid. pple. dadhāna), state of believing:; (both prose).

, adj. (ppp. of Skt. abhi-ṣajati, Pali abhisajati, both offend, give offense to; afflict; cf. abhiṣajyate; wrongly defined in s.v. sañj with abhi; Crit. ed. [tāpito, tāpayet for abhiṣakto, abhiṣajet] and [Rāmakṛṣṇa paraphrases using abhiṣaṅga, glossed parābhava], which are the only two passages cited in; adds one other from, abhiṣakta, defined correctly heimgesucht), (1) lit. offended, hence angered, wrathful (so the cognate Pali abhisaṅgin is used; Pali abhisatta, in most occurrences, = Skt. abhiśapta cursed, but see below), always followed by synonyms kupita, caṇḍībhūta (or in caṇḍīkṛta):; (here krodhābhiṣakta);;; et alibi; (2) in abhiṣaktaḥ defined by Tib. (ṅan ba) and Chin. as simply bad, wicked; the Jap. has three alternative renderings, all obviously based on etymological guesswork; one means vituperated. Occurs in a section entitled krodhakārāḥ, and containing mostly words for anger, angry etc., and perhaps to be interpreted precisely in this sense; in that case belonging with (1). However, Pali abhisattarūpa occurs once (chap. 84 vs. 5;) as ep. of bhūmippadesa, a region, described as desolate, barren wilderness; the comm. and modern interpreters take it as meaning accursed, identifying it with the usual Pali abhisatta (= ˚śapta, above); but the context contains no evidence for this; possibly it = Skt. abhiṣakta, orig. heimgesucht (as in, above), afflicted, evil. In that case abhiṣakta of might mean what Tib. and Chin. say, simply wicked, which would be not a difficult development from afflicted.

, nt. (to Skt. abhi with saj or sañj, in a sense not recorded in Skt., but cf. Pali abhisajjati, a,), perh. sticking fast (together), said of the teeth during the process of eating: (asyāhāraṃ paribhuñjānasya na) … paryavanāho (q.v.) vābhiṣajjanaṃ [Page057-a] (printed vā bhi˚) vā; but 2d ed. vātisarjanaṃ; what atisaṛjana would mean in this context is obscure; excessive emission (spitting out of food)?

(cf. prec. and following entries), (1) overflows with evil emotion, specifically anger or malice: (asurāḥ) kupyanti vyāpadyanti abhiṣyandanti; (2) some form or derivative of this verb is intended in, which misunderstands; the mg. must be becoming inflated (with evil bodily humors), cf. abhiṣyaṇṇa; this condition of the Buddhaʼs body resulted from his first meal after the seven-weeks fast. The next sentence says that Śakra brought harītakī, a purgative medicine, so that his humors might become pacified, restored to ease, dhātūnāṃ sukhaṃ (em. to mukhaṃ by !) bhaviṣyati. The exact reading in 1 is uncertain; possibly tathā abhiṣyanditam, impersonal, inflation, over-exuberance (of humors) was caused.
(nt.; = Pali abhisandana; cf. prec. and next), (over-)flowing: -mahākaruṇābhiṣyandana-tavā, because it is full to overflowing with great compassion.

(ppp. of Skt. abhi-ṣvaj), attached (to, acc.): (prose) jīvitaśarīrāṇy abhiṣvaktānām (em. ˚śarīrābhi˚).

(cf. Skt. abhisaṃrādhana,, once in, defined wohl das Befriedigen, Zufriedenstellen), [Page057-b] applauds: pres. pple. ˚dhayan; ger. ˚dhya;;;.

(= Pali ˚saṃkharoti; recorded in Vedic () as zurechtmachen, bilden,; see abhisaṃkaroti, ˚skṛta, ˚saṃskāra, etc.), accomplishes, performs, does, fashions; often governs acc. of cognate abhisaṃskāra, q.v., in various shades of its meaning; prāsādam abhisaṃskṛtavantaḥ, built a palace; karmābhisaṃskaroti, performs action; with cittam, makes up, fixes (the mind, thought), cittam ˚roti; (bhūmidharma) ˚ronti, (Bodhisattvas in 9th bhūmi) fully realize (in their minds, the conditions or laws of the bhūmi); without object cittam (cf. abhisaṃskāra without citta-, mental determination) uttiṣṭhāmīti cābhisaṃskurvaṃs, making up my mind (Tib. sñam na, thinking) that I would arise (I fell down), cf. s.v. abhisaṃskāra (the situation is the same); but in the parallel uttiṣṭhāmīti gātrāṇy abhisaṃskurvann, preparing (making ready, fixing) my limbs with the intent to arise.

, m. (cited from Skt. only, from; essentially a Buddhist word; = Pali abhisaṃkhāra; see ˚skaroti, ˚skṛta), performance, accomplishment: (udāraṃ dharmābhi˚, noble performance of dharma); in all meanings often made object of the cognate verb ˚skaroti, as pāramitābhisaṃskāraṃ cābhisaṃskaroti, and accomplishes the accomplishment of the Pāramitās; performances; na vyañjanābhisaṃskārārthī, not seeking the accomplishment of the letter (but of the spirit, the true esoteric meaning, arthārthī); often ṛddhyabhi˚ (= Pali iddhābhi˚) performance of magic,;;;;;;; object of the verb ˚skaroti, perform a magic performance,;;;; performance of action, (here specified as karmābhi˚), generally with special reference to its fruits, good or bad, esp. when modified by, or cpd. with, words like puṇya, apuṇya, kuśala, pāpa(ka), the Pali equivalents of which are similarly used; here abhi˚ often may be rendered accumulation, piling up (of merit or demerit), and abhisaṃskaroti accumulates; cf. pāpakān abhisaṃskārān abhisaṃskariṣyanti with puṇyāpuṇyāneñjyān abhisaṃskārān upacinvanti, (ignorant persons) accumulate (upa-ci, unambiguous!) performances (or accumulations, of karman) that are meritorious, demeritorious, or leading to immovable states (see aneñjya), suggesting that the passage means really will accumulate evil accumulations (of karman); so also duḥkhābhisaṃskāra-mala-impurity due to the accumulation (hardly performance!) of miseries (thru karman); puṇyābhi˚ and kuśalābhi˚ together,;;; puṇyābhi˚ also;;; apuṇyābhi˚; kuśalābhi˚; cittābhisaṃskāra, accomplishment of (proper) thoughts or state of mind, right mental make up, ayaṃ pradīpas tayā dārikayā mahatā cittābhisaṃskāreṇa prajvalito (this gives the flame magic power of persistence); same without citta, parivrājikā … visṛṣṭena svareṇābhisaṃskāreṇa (with mental preparation or concentration, application of mind, fixed determination) svādhyāyaṃ karontī; sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca abhisaṃskāreṇa, with careful mental preparation, application, determination (here, to rise up after having fallen down; and so;;; the situation is the same as in where abhisaṃskurvaṃs occurs, see ˚skaroti); see sābhisaṃskāra, in which abhi˚ comes close to this shade of mg.

(= Pali ˚saṃkhata), ppp. of ˚skaroti; see also an-abhi˚; accomplished, effected, formed: [Page058-a] (˚taṃ, jñānaṃ bodhisattvasya), 5; and (cetasā cittam ˚tam, the thought was mentally formed; same omitting cetasā,;); of action, good or bad, with reference to its necessary fruit, accomplished, done, accumulated, stored up, ˚tena (karmaṇā); ˚taṃ (pāpakaṃ karma, pūrve, previously); in tac ca karmābhisaṃskṛtam, merely that action that has been performed.
(m.), abandonment (Tib. bskyur ba; opp. to abhinirhāra): (tatrāyam) ˚ra-samkocaḥ, tatrāyam abhinirhāra-vistaraḥ.
(cf. abhisaṃskaroti), app. honors, treats with respect: śreṣṭhidārakam abhisamkurvanti, jayatu jayatu … śreṣṭhidārako etc.; Tib. mṅon par du byed do (literal; cf.); lit. perhaps makes up properly.

(= Pali ˚saṃkhipati; in Skt. recorded only in mg. compress, by magic into a small size; so used also in BHS, e.g.), subsumes, collects, puts together under one heading: sarvakuśalamūlāny abhisaṃkṣipya tulayitvā piṇḍayitvā; esp. with aikadhyam (so in Skt. aikadhyaṃ saṃsṛjya, and synonyms; in Pali ekajjhaṃ … abhisaṃkhipitvā),;; et alibi;.
(m.; only in the lex. in definition of the Buddhist term middha, q.v.), compression, summary statement: tān aham abhisaṃkṣepād vakṣye.

, fem. to ˚na, adj. (to Pali abhisajati, Skt. ˚ṣajati, see abhiṣajyate, abhiṣakta; cf. Pali parābhisajjanī, s.v. abhisajjanī, used with vācā, offending), offending:, read parābhisañjany (˚nī), with vāk, giving offense to others, for text parābhisaṃjanany (which is uninterpretable).

, m. (= Pali id., in both mgs.; to abhisameti, q.v.), (1) comprehension, clear understanding; (spiritual) realization, intuitive grasp (of religious verities), in Pali especially grasp of the Law (dhamma) or the four noble truths (sacca); Tib. mṅon par rtogs pa, clear comprehension; cf.,, ‘abhisamaya means direct intuition of the Absolute. Here it means the Path of attaining that intuition … a synonym of mārga’; often in comp. with that which is comprehended: dharmābhi˚;;; satyābhi˚ (as in Pali, above); and (in these two saha, preceding satyā˚, should be taken as a separate word);; āryasatyānām abhisamayāya; jñānābhi˚; prāpty-abhi˚ (on prāpti cf. et passim); yogābhi˚; mārgābhi˚ (realization, intuitive comprehension, of the Path); (śrāvaka-, pratyekabuddha-, and tathāgata-)yānābhi˚ (comprehension of the vehicles); of the inferior intuitions or realizations of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;;; used absolutely, something like enlightenment or spiritual realization in general,;;; listed among synonyms of nirvāṇa; abhisamayāntika (see antika), ending in abhi˚ (realization? enlightenment? nirvāṇa?);; abhisamayādhigamajñāna- (enlightenment = an intuitive understanding, for abhisamaya); (2) any of the three collective conversions of crowds of disciples, accomplished by Buddha; [Page058-b] so (and also dhammābhi˚) in Pali, see :;.

(= Pali id.; = abhisameti; in Skt. only in literal sense, comes to), arrives at understanding of (with acc.): āryasatyāni pravicinvato 'bhisamāgacchato (gen. sg. pres. pple.) 'bhisamāgateṣu ca tajjñānam utpadyate.

, m. (nowhere recorded), complete confidence: ˚yaḥ = Tib. mṅon par yid ches (-śes) pa, superior belief; bhagavadvacanābhisaṃpratyayāt, thru reliance on what the Lord said;.

(nt.; n. act. in -ana from abhisaṃbuddhati = ˚budhyati, q.v.), the becoming perfectly enlightened:, in cpd., (praṇidhānam …) anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhy-abhisaṃbuddhana-tāyai.

(on the last two see Chap. 43, s.v. budh; = Pali ˚bujjhati; very rare in Skt., recorded and only once, ppp. ˚buddhaḥ, with atra, well skilled, learned, enlightened on this matter, Crit. ed.; the pres. ˚bodhati implied in ger. ˚bodhitvā), (1) becomes enlightened, attains complete enlightenment (i.e. becomes a Buddha); the common meaning in BHS. Used absolutely: ˚budhyati (v.l. ˚buddhati); fut. ˚bhotsyate; ppp. ˚buddho bhagavān; gdve. ˚boddhavyam one ought to become enlightened;; [Page059-a]. Much more often with ‘cognate’ acc., regularly anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim, unto supreme perfect enlightenment, the subject being a Buddha or other person: ˚budhyate;; opt. ˚budhyeyam; ˚buddheyam; fut. ˚bhotsyasi;; ˚se; ˚sye (1 sg.); ˚syante;;; ˚budhiṣyam (sic!); ˚buddhiṣyati; ˚ṣyasi; ˚ṣyāmi; aor. ˚buddhe; ppp. ˚buddha, still with acc. of complement (anuttarāṃ samyak˚), ˚buddho;; ˚buddho bhaviṣyati; ˚buddhaḥ with complement bodhim; saṃbodhim an-abhisaṃbuddho; (on the same ppp. in passive sense see below;) ger. ˚buddhitvā (anuttarāṃ samvak˚);;; ˚bodhitvā; (here v.l. ˚buddhitvā); inf. ˚boddhukāmena; instead of acc., loc. of same complement, opt. ˚buddheyaṃ (anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau), and ppp. ˚buddhaḥ; the pres. ˚budhyate, the ppp., and the gdve., are also used passively, subject being anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ, and the person put in the instr.: (tathāgatena …) an˚rā samy˚dhir abhisaṃbuddhā, supreme enlightenment was attained, realized; so also;;; pres. ˚budhyate; gdve. ˚boddhavyā; note also the cpd. abhisaṃbuddha-bodhis (tathāgataḥ), the Tathāgata having attained enlightenment; (2) the verb is however also used (as in the isolated Skt. occurrence noted above) in the sense of learns thoroughly, becomes skilled in, comprehends perfectly: asmābhir … tathāgatajñāne abhisaṃboddhavye (loc. abs.), when the Tathāgata knowledge ought to have been realized ({{thoroly learned->thoroughly learned||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}}) by us; (kāyaṃ) marīcidharmaṃ ˚budhānaḥ (so oldest ms., with Pali; later mss. paribudhya caiva, see paribudhyati), learning to know (realizing) the body as having the nature of a mirage; nāsau mārgaḥ śakya evaṃ … ˚boddhum, that Way cannot be realized (made the object of enlightened understanding) in this manner; kaccid evaṃ rūpaṃ sthānam abhisaṃbhotsyase? abhisaṃbhotsye, you will learn perfectly such-and-such a point (of duty), wonʼt you? I will; (3) when the subject is dharma, and perhaps in some other cases, it may not be clear whether the verb means understands or illumines, makes clear; in dharmaḥ abhisaṃbuddho (said by the Buddha shortly after his enlightenment) probably means the Law that I have perfectly comprehended, but possibly made clear (to myself); in tathāgatenāryasmiṃ dharmavinaye madhyamā pratipadā abhisaṃbuddhā, apparently the middle course of conduct, perfectly illumined (made clear) by the Tathāgata in the noble dharma (i.e. sūtras) and vinaya; yas tathāgatena dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddho deśito nidhyāto; yaś ca … tathāgatena dharmo 'bhisambuddho deśto vā, realized (? made clear) or taught; and (4) we even find, in a few curious passages in, the complement anuttarāṃ (or ˚rā) samyaksaṃbodhim (or ˚dhir), as in (1) above, with dharmaḥ … abhisaṃbuddhaḥ; the precise meaning is not too clear: asti sa kaścid dharmo yas tathāgatena dīpaṃkarasya … antikād anuttarāṃ samy˚ ˚bodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ (repeated below), is there any principle which has been realized (comprehended? made clear?), unto supreme perfect enlightenment, by the Tathāgata (taking it) from Dīpaṃkara? (the transl. in, is very loose); nāsti … dharmo yas tathāgatenānuttarāṃ samy˚ ˚bodhim ˚buddhaḥ: and with nom. of complement, asti sa kaścid dharmo yas tathāgatenānuttarā samy˚ ˚bodhir ity abhisaṃbuddhaḥ, … any principle which was realized as (?) … (, known under the name of); perhaps the nom. of the complement (apparently isolated) is a corruption for the acc., used at least twice in such a phrase.

(to prec.; = Pali id.; cf. next two), (1) perfect enlightenment: sukhābhisaṃbodhāya; mahābodher abhisaṃbodhaḥ; (2) perfect comprehension; learning perfectly:; cpd. durabhisaṃbodha, hard to learn perfectly, with inf., durabhisaṃbodhāny araṇyavanaprasthāni … adhyāvastum, … hard to learn to dwell in.

, greets in the sense of confronts, something unpleasant, viz. the evil deeds of former births: taṃ pūrve manuṣyabhūtehi abhisaṃskṛtaṃ abhisaṃmodayitaṃ (so most mss., but one ˚dayitvā, prob. read so!) niyataṃ vedanīyaṃ, that which they formerly accomplished (or accumulated) while men, having confronted, must assuredly be suffered (in hell). em. and renders otherwise.

Despite all this confusion, there is no doubt that we are dealing with essentially one word, with modifications due to diverse influences, including popular etymology and hyper-Sktism., gives the ‘correct form’ as ṛtīyate (which, or rather usually rit˚, is customary in, but I believe occurs nowhere else), and the mg. as er schämt sich; both statements are wrong, I believe.
